run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The requested query's gte bound 2026-06-03T00:00:00 is inside the index's data but the field it names is not: the index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p' has no @timestamp field and no date-typed field at all (mapped properties are ingest_ts keyword, level keyword, message text), so the range on @timestamp matched 0 documents. Re-running the same window on the real timestamp-like field, ingest_ts, with level=ERROR returned exactly 7 matching documents. For comparison the index holds 16 documents in total and 12 of them are level=ERROR, so the 7 are the ERROR documents timestamped 2026-06-03 and the remaining 5 ERROR documents are timestamped 2026-06-02. Two caveats bound this answer: ingest_ts is a keyword, so the range is a lexicographic string comparison rather than a date comparison, and all of this data (2026-06-02/03) lies outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:13:27Z to 2026-11-23T18:13:27Z, so the search tool applied no time filter and these counts cannot be tied to that window. This was a counting question, not a fault investigation, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: The requested query {"bool":{"must":[{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"2026-06-03T00:00:00"}}},{"term":{"level":"ERROR"}}]}}} against index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p' returned total value 0 (relation eq) with 1 successful shard and no failures.

The mappings of index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p' contain only the properties ingest_ts (type keyword), level (type keyword) and message (type text); there is no @timestamp field and no date-typed field in the mapping, which is why the search reported time_filter applied=false and applied no time filter.

Re-running against the actual timestamp-like field, {"bool":{"must":[{"range":{"ingest_ts":{"gte":"2026-06-03T00:00:00"}}},{"term":{"level":"ERROR"}}]}}}, returned total value 7 (relation eq) on index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p'; this is the count of level=ERROR documents at or after 2026-06-03T00:00:00.

Without any time constraint the term query level=ERROR matched 12 documents on index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p' (terms aggregation by level: bucket ERROR doc_count 12, sum_other_doc_count 0), while a match_all returned all 16 documents in the index.

The returned documents show the match split: seven ERROR documents carry ingest_ts values 2026-06-03T08:01:00 through 2026-06-03T08:07:00 (messages 'err today 1'..'err today 7'), five ERROR documents carry ingest_ts 2026-06-02T08:01:00 through 2026-06-02T08:05:00 ('err yest 1'..'err yest 5'), and four INFO documents carry ingest_ts 2026-06-03T09:01:00 through 09:04:00.

The zero result on @timestamp is a missing-field result, not a lack of ERROR logs: 12 level=ERROR documents exist in the same index, and 7 of them satisfy the requested 2026-06-03T00:00:00 lower bound once the bound is applied to ingest_ts.

Because no matched index maps a date field, the tool applied no time filter (time_filter applied=false, field=null) and both the 7-document and 12-document counts derive from documents timestamped 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-03, which are outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:13:27Z to 2026-11-23T18:13:27Z; the counts therefore cannot be attributed to that window.

Map a real date-typed field (for example a date-typed ingest_ts or a proper @timestamp) on the 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p' index so range queries are genuine chronological comparisons and so the search tool can apply its incident-window time filter; today ingest_ts is keyword and the range is a lexicographic string comparison.

gaps: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, so the range gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 is a lexicographic string comparison; it orders correctly for the observed 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss' values, but no date parsing or timezone normalisation was verified.

No date-typed field exists in the index mapping, so no query against this index can be constrained to the authorized window by the search tool; the exact per-window counts inside 2026-10-24T18:13:27Z to 2026-11-23T18:13:27Z are unknown (only that observed document timestamps are 2026-06-02/03).

Only the first 20 documents (16 returned, all of them) were inspected for the sample listing; the 7-count and 12-count totals come from exact 'eq' totals, but retention outside this index and any documents removed before now are unknown.
next_steps: If counts anchored to the incident window are required, confirm whether a date-typed timestamp field exists in another index or was dropped from this mapping before re-querying.
Confirm with the index owner whether ingest_ts values are UTC and whether the keyword format is guaranteed uniform, so lexicographic range semantics remain valid.
